the development of new molecular techniques to detect IGH rearrangments in NHL and the characterization of these rearrangments in relation to the different subgroups of NHL.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IGH gene is involved in the pathogenesis of a majority of NHLs, and the detection of IGH rearrangement by FISH is of great importance in the diagnosis and the classification of NHLs.
FISH analysis is an efficient method to detect IGH gene rearrangements and to characterize the partner chromosome in a large proportion of NHL.
IGH rearrangments are found in about 50 to 60% of NHL, and that the use of metaphase FISH is a valuable complement to conventional karyotyping.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGH rearrangement is an essential step in the pathogenesis of follicular and mantle cell lymphoma, but also diffuse large B-cell, marginal zone, Burkitt's, and plasmacytoma.
the IGH rearrangement is a common feature in NHL, and that the use of a combination of techniques is essential to detect all cases and to identify the chromosomic partner(s) involved.
the use of metaphase FISH is essential to detect and characterize IGH translocations, which are the most frequent genetic alterations in NHL.
